items.stem: Find a point on y-axis which is equidistant from the point A(6, 5) and B(-4, 3).

Answer the following questions on the basis of the graph given below: (i) What are the coordinates of School? (ii) What are the coordinates of Police Station? (iii) What are the coordinates of Hospital? (iv) What are the coordinates of Library?

TRUE / FALSE: (i) The origin is the only common point of the two axes. (ii) In a graph paper, the vertical axis is usually known as the x-axis. (iii) On a graph paper, the positions of the points (1, 4), (4, 1) coincide. (iv) The coordinate axes divide the plane into four parts.
items.answer: (i) True. (ii) False - the vertical axis is the y-axis. (iii) False - (1,4) and (4,1) are different points. (iv) True.

items.stem: Without plotting the points indicate the quadrant in which they will lie, if (i) the ordinate is 1 and abscissa is -1 (ii) the abscissa is -5 and ordinate is -2.
items.answer: (i) (-1, 1) has signs $(-, +)$, so Quadrant II. (ii) (-5, -2) has signs $(-, -)$, so Quadrant III.

items.stem: If the points (2, 1) and (1, -2) are equidistant from the point $(x, y)$, show that $x + 3y = 0$.
On plotting the points O(0, 0), A(3, 0), B(3, 4), C(0, 4) and joining OA, AB, BC and CO. Name the figure obtained? Also find the length of its diagonal.
items.answer: $OA = 3$, $AB = 4$, $BC = 3$ and $CO = 4$. Therefore the figure is a rectangle. Its diagonal $= \sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}} = 5$ units.

items.stem: Taking 0.5 cm as 1 unit, plot the following points on the graph paper: $A(1, 3), B(-3, -1), C(1, -4), D(-2, 3), E(0, -8), F(1, 0)$
items.answer: Plot A(1,3), B(-3,-1), C(1,-4), D(-2,3), E(0,-8) and F(1,0), using the stated scale of $0.5\,\mathrm{cm} = 1$ unit.

items.stem: Three vertices of a rectangle are (3, 2), (-4, 2), and (-4, 5). Plot these points and find the coordinates of the fourth vertex.
items.answer: The missing fourth vertex is (3, 5), because the $x$-coordinates are -4 and 3 and the y-coordinates are 2 and 5.

items.stem: If the point (0, 2) is equidistant from the points (3, k) and (k, 5), find the value of k.
If the distance between the points (4, p) and (1, 0) is 5, then what can be the possible values of p?
items.answer: $\sqrt{(4-1)^{2} + p^{2}} = 5 \Rightarrow 9 + p^{2} = 25 \Rightarrow p^{2} = 16$. Therefore $p = \pm 4$.

items.stem: Find the co-ordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining the points A(2, 6) and $B(10, -10)$ into 4 equal points.
items.answer: The three points dividing A(2,6) to B(10,-10) into four equal parts are (4, 2), (6, -2) and (8, -6).

items.stem: If $A(x, y), B(-2, 3)$ and C(2, 1) form an isosceles triangle with $AB = AC$. Also find the relation between $x$ and y.

Consider the points R(3, 0), $A(0, -2)$, $M(-5, -2)$ and P(-5, 2). If they are joined in the same order, predict: (i) Two sides of RAMP that are perpendicular to each other. (ii) One side of RAMP that is parallel to one of the axes. (iii) Two points that are mirror images of each other in one axis. Which axis will this be? (iv) Now plot the points and verify your predictions.
items.answer: (i) PM ⊥ AM and PR ⊥ MP. (ii) AM is parallel to the $x$-axis; MP is parallel to the y-axis. (iii) No points are mirror images.

items.stem: Rony was reading a Maths magazine in which he saw an interesting figure which was half drawn as shown below. He wishes to draw it completely. Draw again and help him to complete the figure and tell which line of symmetry you use. Along with that mark all the coordinates used in this drawing.
Plot the points A(2, 1), B(-1, 2), C(-2, -1), and D$(1, -2)$ in the coordinate plane. Is ABCD a square? Can you explain why? What is the area of this square?
items.answer: $AB^{2} = BC^{2} = CD^{2} = DA^{2} = 10$, while $AC^{2} = BD^{2} = 20$. Thus all four sides are equal and the diagonals are equal, so ABCD is a square. Area $= \mathrm{side}^{2} = 10$ square units.

items.stem: There are two insects A and B. A is moving from left to right horizontally and B is moving from top to bottom vertically. We have divided their path into unit distance of 1 cm and it looks like a cartesian plane. After tracing path, insect A is at point X and insect B is at point Y as shown in the graph. (i) The coordinate where abscissa is + and ordinate is - lies in which quadrant. (ii) What is the ordinate of any point on x-axis. (iii) What is the distance between both insects?
items.answer: (i) Quadrant IV. (ii) The ordinate of any point on the x-axis is always 0. (iii) Distance $= \sqrt{75}$ unit.

items.stem: The Class IX students of a secondary school in Krishinagar have been allotted a rectangular plot of land for their gardening activity. Saplings of Gulmohar are planted on the boundary at a distance of 1 m from each other. There is a lawn PQRS in the ground as shown in the figure. (a) The coordinates of C, taking A as origin? (b) What are the coordinates of $R$, taking A as origin? (c) What is the length of side of lawn? OR What is the area of lawn?
items.answer: (a) Coordinates of $C = (10, 6)$. (b) Coordinates of $R = (5, 6)$. (c) Length of side of lawn PQRS $= \sqrt{3^{2} + 5^{2}} = \sqrt{34}\,\mathrm{m} \approx 5.83\,\mathrm{m}$. OR Area of lawn $= \frac{1}{2} \times d_{1} \times d_{2} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 6 = 30\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

items.stem: To conduct Sports Day activities, in your rectangular shaped school ground ABCD, lines have been drawn with chalk powder at a distance of 1 m each. 100 flower pots have been placed at a distance of 1 m from each other along AD, as shown in the figure. Hema runs 1/4th the distance AD in the 2nd line and posts a blue flag. Preeti runs 1/5th the distance AD on the 8th line and posts a green flag. (a) Which mathematical concept is used in the above problem? (b) What is the position of blue flag and green flag? (c) What is the distance between both the flags? OR If Uttara has to post an orange flag exactly halfway between the line segment joining the two flags, where should she post her flag?
items.answer: (a) Cartesian coordinate system (coordinate geometry). (b) Position of the flags: blue flag (2, 25), green flag (8, 20). (c) Distance between the two flags: $\sqrt{61}$ units. OR Orange flag: (5, 22.5).

items.stem: Once an Archaeologist was doing research in a cave where he got a map to find treasure. So he went in search of the treasure. But when he reached there his map fell into the water and everything vanished from the map. On the other side the Bandit knows the way to reach there but the Police is behind him to catch him. (1 unit on the map = 1 km). (i) Find the coordinates of the treasure. (ii) What are the coordinates of the police officer? (iii) Find the shortest distance between the archaeologist and the treasure. OR (iv) Find the distance between the police officer and the bandit.
items.answer: (i) Coordinates of the Treasure: (7, 14). (ii) Coordinates of the Police officer: (10, 7). (iii) Archaeologist is at (2, 2), Treasure is at (7, 14). $d = \sqrt{(7-2)^{2} + (14-2)^{2}} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13$. The shortest distance is 13 km. OR (iv) The distance between the police officer and the bandit is $\sqrt{26}$ km.
